# J7 — Assemble `JiraDataCenterBackend` and hold it to the backend contract suite

## Context / Problem

With the shared Jira-family layer, the two codecs, the two identity models, and the DC transport in place, the
DC backend itself is an assembly — but it must actually be *proven*. ADR 0035's "Proof-of-seam" makes the
backend-agnostic contract suite the artifact that certifies a backend, and
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` parametrizes its `backend` fixture over
`["fake", "jira"]`. PR #120 added registry and transport tests but never touched that fixture, so its new
backend was never held to the port contract at all.

## What J6 already landed (scope correction, measured against `origin/main` fdc2695a1)

This story's Scope was written before J6 [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56] executed, and J6's change 1049 delivered
more than this plan anticipated. Verified against the merged tree, NOT assumed:

* `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` **already exists** (273 LOC) with `JiraDataCenterBackend`, the
  `@register("jira-datacenter")` factory, and `_search_users_by_username`;
* `adapters/__init__.py` **already imports** the DC backend (line 16), so `select_backend("jira-datacenter")`
  resolves — J6 pins that with its own registry test.

So this story is NOT "write the backend". It is the part J6 could not do: **make the backend reachable through
config, make it actually satisfy the `Backend` port, and hold it to the contract suite.**

## The port-conformance defect this story must fix (measured, not inferred)

`isinstance(JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=...), Backend)` is **`False` on merged `main` today.** The
`Backend` `@runtime_checkable` Protocol (`_backend.py`) requires nine members; the DC backend defines seven and
is missing **`query_project`** and **`assert_env_ready`**, both of which Cloud's `JiraBackend` implements
(`adapters/jira/backend.py:162` and `:169`). Probed directly:

```
vendor True | project True | query_project False | assert_env_ready False
```

This is a production defect, not test bookkeeping, and it is precisely what the contract suite exists to catch
— J6's registry test passed while the backend does not satisfy the port:

* **`query_project`** is the backend's configured READ/query scope, with NO create-time default applied. The
  inbound fetcher scopes its search to it and **fails closed on an empty/invalid value rather than querying
  every project** (bug 626d). Absent, the fetcher raises `AttributeError` on any DC inbound pass.
* **`assert_env_ready`** is the fail-fast that raises the neutral `BackendEnvError` naming the missing
  connection essential BEFORE the transport is used in bootstrap-band execution, instead of a cryptic
  downstream failure (ticket 97f2).

Adding `jira-datacenter` to the contract fixture makes `test_isinstance_backend_facade` go RED until both are
implemented. The suite is the oracle: **the fix belongs in `backend.py`, and no assertion may be weakened to
accommodate the backend.**

## Approach

Widen `reconciler.backend`'s `_as_choice` set to `{"jira", "jira-datacenter"}` and update the field comment,
closing the registered-but-unreachable gap. Implement the two missing `Backend` members on
`JiraDataCenterBackend`, mirroring Cloud's semantics but resolving through DC's own
`resolve_jira_datacenter_settings()` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py`) rather than Cloud's
`acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings`:

* `query_project` returns `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings().project` with **no default substituted** — empty
  when unset, so the fetcher fails closed exactly as Cloud does;
* `assert_env_ready` raises `BackendEnvError` naming whichever of the DC connection essentials is missing —
  the base URL (`[tool.rebar.reconciler].base_url`) and the env-only `JIRA_PAT` — matching Cloud's message
  shape ("missing … configuration: …").

`JiraDataCenterBackend` already composes the shared layer [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `WikiTextCodec`
[rebar:aac8-b283-22c1-4e66], `NameIdentity` [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], and the DC transport
[rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56]; it advertises `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and
deliberately **not** `SupportsIncremental` — DC gets a full inbound scan in v1, since incremental fetch is an
optimization with its own correctness surface and no client need yet. This story asserts that omission so it
cannot be added by accident.

Provenance follows the epic's decision: DC-created tickets carry the shared `jira` creation channel and
`jira-` local-id prefix, with the deployment distinguished by `RemoteRef.instance`. Nothing in the store
vocabulary changes, so no migration and no compatibility gate are involved.

**Then extend `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture params to include the DC backend** (constructed with an
injected fake transport, exactly as `JiraBackend` already is at that fixture), so every generic port assertion
runs against it.

**Alternative rejected:** adapter-local tests only (PR #120). They prove the adapter does what its author
expected, not that it satisfies the port the core drives.

## Scope

- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`** — implement the two missing
  `Backend` members, `query_project` and `assert_env_ready` (see the port-conformance section above). This is
  the file the contract suite's RED test drives; it was absent from an earlier draft of this Scope.
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen the `reconciler.backend` `_as_choice` set (currently `{"jira"}`) and
  update the field comment. **Use a symbol search, not the line number** that an earlier draft of this Scope
  carried (`:697`): the file has changed since, and the validator now sits near `:604`. J6 already owns the DC
  *connection* settings in this file (TLS/`allow_insecure`, `ca_bundle`, `resolved_statuses`); this story owns
  ONLY the backend-choice widening.
- **`tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`** — the dedicated config-validator module (it already
  exists, 2.5K, and already covers default/explicit-jira/unknown-key/env-override). The new
  `jira-datacenter` load case, the env-override case, and the `"jira-server"` rejection case all belong HERE,
  alongside their siblings — not in a new module. Note its existing
  `test_unknown_backend_rejected_at_config_load` asserts `"jira" in str(exc.value)`, which still holds after
  the widening, so it needs no edit.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` — fixture params.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` — **decided, not deferred:** the existing `FakeTransport`
  is what the DC fixture uses. It already satisfies every `TicketTransport` member the contract assertions
  reach. It lacks `probe_remote`, which the backend delegates, but NO contract assertion calls it, and
  `SupportsAbsenceProbe` conformance is satisfied by the *backend's* own `probe_remote`, not the transport's.
  So: **add a one-line `probe_remote` to `FakeTransport`** (so the delegation is exercisable and the fake
  matches the surface the DC backend delegates to) and do **not** introduce a rival DC-specific fake.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` — the reciprocal import rule. The J2
  checker already rejects `adapters/jira/` importing `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (the `_is_within(package,
  _JIRA)` branch in `_violations`), but there is **no rule for the other direction**: a DC module importing
  `adapters/jira/` passes today. That is the half this story adds.
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — add `jira` to the clean-core-wheel absent-module list at line 86
  (today `langchain`, `langgraph`, `anthropic`, `inspect_ai`, `opentelemetry`). Verified safe: `jira` is
  declared ONLY in the `jira-datacenter` extra (`pyproject.toml:168`); the base `dependencies` are just
  `pyyaml`, `jsonschema`, `referencing`, and the `"jira"` at `pyproject.toml:24` is a *keyword*, not a dep.
- **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`** (new) — note the path. An earlier draft said
  `tests/live_jira_dc/`, which does not exist; J5 [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] landed the harness under
  `tests/external/`, the only tier fenced off from per-commit CI. A live test outside it is collected by the
  default suite on runners with no Docker, no Jira and no egress, breaking CI for everyone. Landing under the
  right path also inherits the tier's three mechanisms: the auto-applied `external` marker, the
  `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` opt-in, and the module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel that enrols the module in the
  all-skip canary — so this file MUST define one. J6 additionally established that a live module must FAIL
  LOUDLY (not skip) when the harness is reachable but the `[jira-datacenter]` extra is absent, because the
  canary counts collected-vs-executed globally and a sibling module's executing tests will otherwise mask an
  all-skip; **reuse the exact guard already written in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`**
  (`_live_jira_ready` / `_jira_extra_installed` / `_extra_missing_but_harness_up` /
  `_fail_if_extra_missing_while_harness_is_up`) rather than reinventing it.
  **Local-side provisioning is settled, not left to the executor:** a reconcile pass needs a local ticket
  store, a git repo and a rebar config, which the DC harness conftest does not provision (it owns only the
  Jira side — project, PAT, issue teardown). The `rebar_repo` fixture that
  `tests/external/test_reconcile_live.py` uses is defined in **`tests/external/conftest.py:159`**, the PARENT
  conftest, so `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` **inherits it by ordinary pytest conftest inheritance**. Use it
  directly together with the DC harness's `jira_dc_project` / `jira_dc_pat` fixtures. No new
  `rebar_repo`-equivalent is to be written.
  **But `rebar_repo` alone is NOT sufficient, and the wiring is specified here rather than left to the
  executor.** That fixture calls `rebar.init_repo()` and writes NO `[tool.rebar.reconciler]` config, so the
  reconcile subprocess would have no backend, no base URL and no credential — it would fail at config-load or
  silently drive the Cloud backend. The test MUST therefore, before reconciling:
  1. write a `rebar.toml` into the `rebar_repo` root containing `[reconciler]` with
     `backend = "jira-datacenter"`, `base_url = <the harness base URL>`, and **`allow_insecure = true`** —
     the latter is REQUIRED, not optional: the harness is `http://localhost:2990/jira`
     (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:56`, overridable via `JIRA_DC_BASE_URL`), and J6's TLS
     validator in `_config_schema.py` REJECTS a non-`https` base URL at config-load time unless
     `allow_insecure` is set. Also write `[jira]` with `project = <jira_dc_project>`, which is where
     `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings()` reads the project from;
  2. `monkeypatch.setenv("JIRA_PAT", jira_dc_pat)` — `jira_dc_pat` returns a raw token STRING and sets no
     environment variable itself. This does reach the child process: `rebar._engine.engine_env` builds the
     subprocess environment as `dict(os.environ)` (`_engine.py:93`), so the PAT propagates.

## Testing

Contract tier for the port, plus a live end-to-end pass on the J5 harness [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] because this story is
the point at which the whole assembly first drives a real instance.

- contract: every existing assertion in `test_backend_contract.py` passes with the DC backend in the fixture
  params, unmodified — the suite is the oracle and must not be weakened to accommodate the new backend.
- port conformance (RED-first): `test_isinstance_backend_facade` is asserted to FAIL before `query_project` /
  `assert_env_ready` exist and PASS after — the defect is demonstrated, not merely fixed.
- `query_project` / `assert_env_ready` behaviour, in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`: `query_project` returns
  the configured project and returns **empty** (not a default) when unset, so the fetcher's fail-closed
  contract holds; `assert_env_ready` raises `BackendEnvError` naming each missing essential and returns
  cleanly when all are present.
- capability: `isinstance` checks confirm `Backend`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`,
  `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and confirm it is NOT `SupportsIncremental` (the deliberate omission, asserted so it
  cannot be added by accident).
- config, in `tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`: `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` loads;
  the `REBAR_RECONCILER_BACKEND=jira-datacenter` env override resolves; an unknown key still raises
  `ConfigError` naming the valid choices.
- import contract: the new reciprocal rule has TEETH — a synthetic DC-imports-Cloud source is asserted to be
  flagged, mirroring how J2's `test_checker_flags_a_synthetic_violation` proves its own direction, with the
  permitted `jira_datacenter -> jira_family` direction retained as a negative control.
- live end-to-end: a full reconcile pass against the harness creates a remote issue from a local ticket,
  round-trips a status change and a comment inbound, and a second pass is a **no-op** — idempotence is the
  postcondition that proves convergence rather than mere writing.
- provenance oracle: asserted in the **live** module (`test_reconcile_pass.py`), since only a real pass
  produces a genuinely DC-created local ticket — a DC-created local ticket has `creation_channel == "jira"`
  and a `jira-`-prefixed id, and its `RemoteRef.instance` names the DC deployment, pinning the epic's
  shared-identity decision.
- error path: a transport failure PROPAGATES — asserted at the unit tier with `pytest.raises`, driving a fake
  transport that raises on a write. **One behaviour, one assertion style:** the criterion is satisfied by
  propagation only; a caught-and-logged variant does NOT satisfy it, so there is no "or" for an executor to
  resolve.
- zero-unhandled-exceptions mechanism (live): **not `caplog`.** `rebar.reconcile()` runs the reconciler in a
  SUBPROCESS (`subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)`, `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:114`), and `caplog` hooks
  only the *test* process's `logging`, so it can never see those records — and on the success path
  `reconcile()` returns parsed stdout JSON and discards stderr entirely. The live test therefore invokes the
  reconciler subprocess DIRECTLY — the same argv `_lib_ops.reconcile` builds
  (`[sys.executable, "-m", "rebar_reconciler", "--mode", <mode>, "--repo-root", <root>]`, with
  `env=rebar._engine.engine_env(root)`) — with `capture_output=True`, then asserts on the captured streams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` implements `query_project`, and `isinstance(backend, Backend)` is asserted
      `True`
- [ ] `query_project` returns the EMPTY string when the project is unset — no create-time default
      substituted — preserving the inbound fetcher's fail-closed contract (bug 626d)
- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` implements `assert_env_ready`, which raises `BackendEnvError` naming each
      missing DC connection essential and returns cleanly when all are present
- [ ] `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes with no assertion
      weakened (`git diff` shows params-only change to that file)
- [ ] a test asserts the backend is NOT an instance of `SupportsIncremental`
- [ ] `FakeTransport` in `backend_support.py` exposes `probe_remote`, and a test asserts the DC backend's
      `probe_remote` DELEGATES to it (observed via the fake's recorded `calls`)
- [ ] [operator-attested] a full reconcile pass against the J5 harness converges, and an immediately repeated pass writes nothing
      (idempotence), with both pass logs attached as a ticket comment
- [ ] a DC-created ticket is asserted — in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — to carry
      `creation_channel == "jira"` and a populated `RemoteRef.instance`
- [ ] `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` loads, asserted in
      `tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`
- [ ] the `REBAR_RECONCILER_BACKEND=jira-datacenter` env override resolves, asserted in the same module
- [ ] `reconciler.backend = "jira-server"` still raises `ConfigError` listing the valid choices
- [ ] the import-contract test from J2 is EXTENDED to cover the now-existing `adapters/jira_datacenter/`
      package: no module under it imports from `adapters/jira/`, and `adapters/jira_family/` imports from
      neither adapter — this is the reciprocal half J2 could not assert because the package did not exist yet
- [ ] `jira` is added to the absent-module list in `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`'s clean-core-wheel
      check (which today covers only `langchain`, `langgraph`, `anthropic`, `inspect_ai`, `opentelemetry`), so
      a future change that leaks the DC dependency into the base install fails CI
- [ ] the live bidirectional pass asserts ZERO unhandled exceptions by invoking the reconciler SUBPROCESS
      directly (`[sys.executable, "-m", "rebar_reconciler", "--mode", …, "--repo-root", …]` under
      `engine_env`, `capture_output=True`) and asserting `returncode == 0`, `"Traceback" not in stderr`, and
      `mutation_failures == 0` in the parsed stdout envelope — `caplog` is NOT usable here because the
      reconciler runs in a subprocess (`_lib_ops.py:114`), and a swallowed exception can still converge
      (epic AC6)
- [ ] a DC transport failure on a write PROPAGATES out of the call, asserted with `pytest.raises` against a
      fake transport that raises — it is not swallowed into a converged pass
